precepts.text: Purge out the old leaven that ye may be a new lump, for Christ our passover is sacrificed for us. To be a faithful steward you have to purge the old leaven out of yourself.
precepts.point: Let a man account of us as ministers of Christ and stewards of the mysteries of God. It is required in stewards that a man be found faithful.

note.label: Much Is Given, Much Is Required

precepts.why:
“Let a man so account of us, as of the ministers of Christ, and stewards of the mysteries of God. Moreover it is required in stewards, that a man be found faithful.” In a steward you have to be found faithful. How?

“Purge out therefore the old leaven, that ye may be a new lump, as ye are unleavened. For even Christ our passover is sacrificed for us”. If you want to be a minister of God, you have to purge out the old leaven. You cannot be moving with old leaven inside of you. Christ died for our sin, so we have to purge it out.

Paul says the same to the Corinthians again: “Wherefore come out from among them, and be ye separate, saith the Lord, and touch not the unclean thing; and I will receive you, And will be a Father unto you, and ye shall be my sons and daughters”. Then: “Having therefore these promises, dearly beloved, let us cleanse ourselves from all filthiness of the flesh and spirit, perfecting holiness in the fear of God.” Cleanse yourself and you are new: “if any man be in Christ, he is a new creature: old things are passed away; behold, all things are become new.”

That is the faithful steward: a man who has purged the old leaven out of himself, so that he does not live in hypocrisy, teaching the people to come out of the world while he himself does not live it.

precepts.text: God hath set forth us the apostles last, as it were appointed to death, a spectacle unto the world. That is the cost. Do you want to die as an apostle found faithful, or run the whole race and hear him say I never knew you?
precepts.point: Let a man account of us as ministers of Christ and stewards of the mysteries of God. It is required in stewards that a man be found faithful.

note.label: Much Is Given, Much Is Required

precepts.why:
“For I think that God hath set forth us the apostles last, as it were appointed to death: for we are made a spectacle unto the world, and to angels, and to men.” This is the cost to pay: we are going to be a spectacle, and we are appointed unto death.

So do you want to die as an apostle with the old leaven still living in you, or do you want to die as an apostle found faithful? Otherwise you say, Lord, Lord, did I not prophesy in your name, and he says, I don't know you. Then why are you doing this? To run this whole race and not get it?

Much is given, much is required. The Lord gave you understanding and shared it with you; where is the return? Are you playing games, treating this Bible like a joke? He will say, I gave you a lot of understanding, now I will punish you accordingly because you knew better: you were profitable to many, but not profitable to yourself.

We persuade men because we know the terror of the Lord, and we cleanse ourselves in the fear of God. That is why the steward must be found faithful: we are appointed to death as a spectacle to the world, and only the faithful steward receives the promise.

precepts.text: Judge nothing before the time, until the Most High brings to light the hidden things and makes manifest the counsels of the hearts.
precepts.point: This is the true meaning of loving your enemies. Christianity twists it to mean love the ones who enslaved, raped, and colonized your ancestors, stole your nationality, land, and heritage, miseducated you, gave you a false image of God, and today shut down anyone who says Israel is the true children of God. That is not the enemy the scripture means. The Bible means love the enemies within your own nation, because Paul, who persecuted and killed the disciples, was one of those enemies who could still repent.
precepts.why:
Ananias had heard by many how much evil Saul had done to the saints at Jerusalem. Saul had consented to Stephen's death and chased the disciples from city to city with zeal. Was he doing it in ignorance? Yes. That is why the scripture says, “judge nothing before the time, until the Lord come, who both will bring to light the hidden things of darkness, and will make manifest the counsels of the hearts”.

The things we all did in the world were worthy of death, so who are we to say a man is beyond repentance? The killer, even a pastor putting us to death in the future, may come to the truth later and say he did it in ignorance, as Christ and Stephen both prayed, Father, forgive them. Even a sister who cursed the teacher out on the streets for months came around and began to listen, because anyone can repent. Leave the judging to the Most High, who will make manifest the counsels of the hearts.

note.label: Final Call: Message to the Black Man

points: Read that part again. That ye might learn what? That ye might learn in us. You may learn in us, the leaders, not to think of men above that which is written. Don't think of us above that which is written. Watch this.

That no one of you be puffed up for one against another. That no one of you be puffed up against one another. What will happen? You begin to think you're better than your brother. You think you high and mighty. You are of a certain status and everybody else is beneath you. That's what happens. No. In other words, it's really an insult for me to say to y'all, none of this is possible without me. What does it say about y'all? Y'all can't do nothing without me. Y'all are nobody without me. Damn. That's really what I'm saying. Y'all see that? Now, I got another one. Uh oh. Matthew 3 and 9.

note.label: From Negroes to Gods from Earth to Gold

points: Let a man so account of us, as of the ministers of Christ, and stewards of the mysteries of God. That is who we are. We are declaring the mysteries of God. We are the stewards.

Moreover it is required in stewards, that a man be found faithful. But with me it is a very small thing that I should be judged of you, or of man's judgment: yea, I judge not mine own self. For I know nothing by myself; yet am I not hereby justified: but he that judgeth me is the Lord.

Therefore judge nothing before the time, until the Lord come, who both will bring to light the hidden things of darkness, and will make manifest the counsels of the hearts. Because some of you all are hiding stuff. But it says the Lord will make known the hidden things of the heart. And then shall every man have praise of God.

You ever see some of the camps, you see the same teacher all the time? That is not with us. Any state you go to, whoever is over that state, those men are known. There is one camp where all you see is this one person from the camp. He is all over social media. You do not even see the leader the way you see him. You do not see no other teacher. That whole camp is weak, because you only let one man speak. Paul was against that. Everybody should be nice with the scriptures, no matter what state we go to. You should not just keep seeing one person from the organisation doing every single debate. We know if someone asks for a debate in Michigan and California and Washington, we have got men there.

And these things, brethren, I have in a figure transferred to myself and to Apollos for your sakes; that ye might learn in us not to think of men above that which is written. Because some people take these secrets and the understanding that they have, and they think they are better than each other. We are not supposed to do that. Even though the ministries are against us, we still want to sit down with them and teach them. They have the arrogance, like we are beneath them to speak to them. So like I will be saying in the clubhouse, if you all come humble and you all come to learn, I am going to match your energy. But if you all come with arrogance and you all are trying to set us up or try to make us look stupid, you are going to get that work.

That no one of you be puffed up for one against another. Because they knew a lot. So it is easy to look at a man, because he knows the mysteries, he knows the secrets, and think they are so great. We have got to be humble with each other. You see how we are eager? We call you guys, come. We want to tell you what we know, because we want you guys to grow.

For who maketh thee to differ from another? and what hast thou that thou didst not receive? now if thou didst receive it, why dost thou glory, as if thou hadst not received it? Now ye are full, now ye are rich, ye have reigned as kings without us: and I would to God ye did reign, that we also might reign with you. Because when you do good, we do good. And that is what Paul was saying. Even though we are stewards of God and these mysteries, these secrets, have been given to each other, we are all on the same level. If I do not know something, I am going to tell you.

But with me it is a very small thing that I should be judged of you, or of man's judgment. The Corinthians ran their mouths about Paul behind his back, because Paul had a past: he hunted the believers down. But the Lord called him out of that, and Paul said, I do not care what you think of me.

note.label: Blasphemers & Traitors: Judge Not Before the Time

points: Yea, I judge not mine own self; he that judgeth me is the Lord. Therefore judge nothing before the time, until the Lord come, who both will bring to light the hidden things of darkness, and will make manifest the counsels of the hearts: and then shall every man have praise of God.
Judge nothing, and no one, before the time; because what happened to somebody yesterday can happen to you today.

note.label: Blasphemers & Traitors: Judge Not Before the Time

points: God hath set forth us the apostles last, as it were appointed to death: for we are made a spectacle unto the world. That is what the hiders do not want: they want to be Israelites in the background. No; if you are in this truth, you are a light that shines on a mountaintop. You cannot blend in. That is why they want the camps gone, because the camps put this truth in the forefront. You are going to die in the background too.

note.label: Traitors and Their Exquisite Subtlety: The Judas Iscariot Effect

points: We are fools for Christ's sake; we are weak; we are despised; being reviled, we bless; being persecuted, we suffer it: being defamed, we intreat. Reviled means slandered and lied on; defamed is being labeled hateful and phobic. We are made as the filth of the world, the offscouring of all things unto this day. Rejected, but the Lord does not reject us; the Lord has our back.

note.label: Traitors and Their Exquisite Subtlety: The Judas Iscariot Effect

points: God hath set forth us the apostles last. Before us came Pedro Albizu Campos, Blanca Canales, Lolita Lebron, Filiberto Ojeda Rios, the Young Lords, all the brothers and sisters who paved the way and fought for our rights. It was not just the southern kingdom fighting in the 60s; the northern kingdom was fighting as well.

Albizu Campos passed away April 21st, 1965, and four days later there was a revolution in the Dominican Republic the same year. There were always revolts in Cuba, in Haiti, in the Dominican Republic, in Puerto Rico, because we are not a people that is supposed to be enslaved or indoctrinated.

The Most High left the apostles last, as it is to this day. People are going to laugh at the men in purple and gold, but the scriptures prove who we are. God left the truth so that we can find it and plant it in the hearts and minds of our people. We have a big job to do.

note.label: Puerto Rico: The Flame Of Resistance

note.label: Much Is Given, Much Is Required

points: God hath set forth us the apostles last, as it were appointed to death. The Nation of Islam, Marcus Garvey, Martin Luther King, the Black Panthers, the Young Lords and AIM all rose up under oppression, and our people are in the same condition. God left the apostles for last: the 144,000, planting the seed of God in the hearts of our people.
Appointed to death: the apostles are here in the last days and will die doing this work, as Garvey and Malcolm X were killed.
